title: Beef Tacos
subtitle: seasoned beef mince in corn or flour tortillas
excerpt: Spiced beef mince cooked with onion, garlic, and a rich tomato base. It goes into warm tortillas with grated cheddar, soured cream, and a squeeze of lime. A fast, crowd-pleasing weeknight meal.
sourceNotes: Tacos with beef mince became popular in the United States through the mid-20th century as Mexican-American communities spread the dish beyond its regional origins. Today they are a staple across both countries.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked beef mince without toppings.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the beef and freeze half for another meal.

content.text: Drain the fat from the mince after browning, or the filling will be greasy. Add the spices after the onion softens so they cook in the oil and release their flavour.
Cook the onion in a little oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Turn up the heat. Add the beef mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 5 minutes until browned.
Drain any excess fat from the pan. Add the tinned tomatoes and stir well.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season with salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Fill with beef, grated cheddar, soured cream, and a squeeze of lime.

items.fix: Tilt the pan and spoon out excess fat after browning the mince before adding the tomatoes.

items.cause: Too much liquid or not simmered enough
items.fix: Simmer uncovered until the liquid reduces and the mixture holds its shape when spooned.

items.cause: Added too late or not cooked in the oil
items.fix: Add dry spices to the pan before the mince so they fry briefly in the oil for 30 to 60 seconds.

content.text: Beef tacos are a staple of Mexican home cooking that spread widely through the United States from the mid-20th century onward. The quick-cook mince version became popular in Mexican-American households and eventually found its way into mainstream American culture. Today they are eaten in homes and restaurants across the world. In Mexico, the range of taco fillings is far wider than most people outside the country realise.
